Show the progress inside one analysis

Source: R/progress.R
progress.Rd

progress() shows how far a long analysis is, for example a bootstrap loop, on the line of its scenario in the display of run_plan(). Outside a run of run_plan() it only checks its arguments.

Usage

progress(done, total, label = NULL)

Arguments

done

The number of steps done, one number of 0 or more.

total

The number of steps of the analysis, one number of 1 or more.

label

Optional. A short text, for example "bootstrap".

Value

NULL, invisibly.

Details

Call progress() in the loop of an action function. The line of the scenario then shows the kind of the analysis, the values of its extra dimensions, label, done/total and the percent. When at least 3 steps and at least 10% of the steps are done, it also shows the time left. That time comes from the rate of the steps of this analysis. The count of the finished analyses of the scenario does not change.

After the first failed analysis of the run, no new analysis starts, and an analysis that runs goes on to its end. Its calls of progress() still show.

progress() drops a call less than 0.5 seconds after the last one that it showed. So a call in each pass of a fast loop costs little. It checks its arguments at each call, also outside run_plan(), so a wrong argument stops the analysis however fast it runs.

Apart from the check of its arguments, progress() does nothing in these cases:

  • outside run_plan(), for example when you step through an analysis by hand, or call the action function yourself.

  • in a data function.

  • in a forked child process, for example inside parallel::mclapply(). Several children would write to the one connection of the worker at the same time. Call progress() in the loop of the analysis itself, for example between chunks of the replicates, as the example shows.

See also

vignette("pbn"), whose section Progress shows the display.

Other plan: add_analyses(), add_data(), cohort_data(), get_data(), run_plan()

Examples

fit_boot <- function(data, argset) {
  n_boot <- 200
  chunks <- split(seq_len(n_boot), ceiling(seq_len(n_boot) / 50))
  est <- numeric(0)
  for (chunk in chunks) {
    # With forks, for example parallel::mclapply(chunk, ...), call
    # progress() here, between the chunks.
    est <- c(est, vapply(chunk, function(b) {
      return(mean(sample(data$d$x, replace = TRUE)))
    }, numeric(1)))
    pbn::progress(length(est), n_boot, "bootstrap")
  }
  return(data.frame(estimate = mean(data$d$x), se = stats::sd(est)))
}
# Outside run_plan(), progress() does nothing, so this call returns the
# value at once.
fit_boot(list(d = data.frame(x = stats::rnorm(20))), list())
#>    estimate        se
#> 1 0.2756986 0.2659695
